quarterly_data.signal: Core Scientific co-founder and Chief Development Officer Russell Cann on the H.C. Wainwright panel: its first AI deal (February 2024) was a small leased air-cooled site converted from 5-7 kW racks to 17-20 kW racks to run H100s / H200s in about a 45-day conversion; the CoreWeave deal followed in June 2024, and since then Core Scientific has turned on and is building 'like 450, 500 megawatts'. Build cost for direct-liquid-cooled capacity: 'around $4.5 million a megawatt' in the late-2023 estimates, 'just under $8 million a megawatt' when the deal was inked in June 2024, '$10 million-$10.5 million a megawatt' for the sites turned on this year and 'between $12 million and $13 million a megawatt' for the sites turning on in 2027 - most of the increase in labor and in gear such as switchgear and transformers. He named labor as a key roadblock (journeyman electricians on its sites make about $250,000-$350,000 a year, master electricians about $750,000) alongside power at the site, NIMBY and long-lead equipment.
quarterly_data.figure: build cost ~$4.5M/MW (late-2023 estimate), just under $8M/MW (June 2024), $10M-$10.5M/MW (sites turned on this year), $12M-$13M/MW (sites turning on in 2027); 450-500 MW turned on or being built

quarterly_data.signal: Core Scientific CDO Russell Cann's view of demand (H.C. Wainwright panel): 'There's about 5 gigawatts of rack space being delivered every year, and there's about 15 gigawatts of chip demand every year'; the companies delivering rack space and chips are not the bubble - speculative data-center requests are (Texas had 474 gigawatts of data-center requests). He sees small inference sites in high demand, especially from labs that need inference load, alongside very large campuses, and expects Core Scientific to have some smaller deals coming as well; he said Core Scientific is one of the largest users of power in ERCOT.
quarterly_data.figure: about 5 GW of rack space delivered per year vs about 15 GW of chip demand per year; 474 GW of data-center requests in Texas

contracts.signal: Core Scientific CDO Russell Cann (H.C. Wainwright panel): the AMD deal announced about six weeks earlier was for about 500 megawatts; on signing, Core Scientific agreed to give AMD the next 2,000 megawatts at three of its own sites (Hunt County, Texas; Pecos, Texas; Muskogee, Oklahoma), where the power is in place, and he expects AMD to take all 2,000 megawatts 'unless the market just really goes south'. Lease economics: 'a triple net lease at 125, or it is a modified gross at 145 MRC, for 15 years with AMD, which is where the market is right now'.
contracts.units: about 500 MW signed; next 2,000 MW at Hunt County, Pecos and Muskogee

contracts.signal: Core Scientific CDO Russell Cann (H.C. Wainwright panel): the CoreWeave deal, signed in June 2024, carries 'about $5 billion in NRC, and it is $100 MRC, meaning CoreWeave put up a lot of the capital for building out those sites' - economics he contrasted with the later AMD lease.

quarterly_data.signal: Bitdeer CFO Michael Potter on the H.C. Wainwright panel: in its GPU-as-a-service business in Malaysia, customers (investment grade or near investment grade) advance 'about 50% or more of the GPU cost' as a prepayment on the service payments they will make, which he said cuts Bitdeer's financing need by 50% or more and lets it scale with less capital; the deployments go into sites leased from another provider in Malaysia, executing early next year into mid next year. 'It's $800 million in more revenue just for the first 10 megawatts over five years', growing from 10 to 20 to 65 megawatts.
quarterly_data.figure: customers prepay about 50% or more of GPU cost; $800 million more revenue for the first 10 megawatts over five years
